codex.worst_flaw: Launch should wait until an independent check confirms that dispatch records and offline device timestamps reliably establish whether the checklist was completed before work actually began.

claude.worst_flaw: The staggered-crew comparison has no predefined sample size, uncertainty handling, cost/harm decision thresholds or spillover controls. holistic.reason: Unusually well-designed for a unionised workforce, with pilot fixes, steward agreement, rewards for stop-work, quality sampling and a default-to-checklist exit, though a 30-minute paid release is a modest incentive and may be low-salience, and lasting effects depend on the app-default change actually removing friction.

codex.worst_flaw: Using the approved safety fallback during an outage lowers the crew’s chance of earning the break, creating peer pressure to avoid the fallback.

claude.worst_flaw: The crew-level 70% milestone gates everyone's break on peers' completion without addressing low-volume technicians, case mix across job types, or a staffed appeal path, and the learning design relies on an optional comparison with no predefined sample size, uncertainty handling or cost/harm decision thresholds.

holistic.reason: Unusually thorough on union co-design, safety-stop protection, gaming safeguards and a default-based exit, but the reward is a modest 30-minute pooled break that may be weakly salient, and durability rests mostly on app fixes and the default screen rather than the reward.

claude.worst_flaw: The credit rule counts a timestamp-valid checklist without real-time verification that the answers reflect the site, and the weekly audit of 10 random checklists across roughly 300 technicians is too thin to catch backfilled or rote ticking before rewards are paid.

codex.worst_flaw: Launch should wait until the programme can independently verify that critical hazards are checked before work starts and has a defined safety response when an audit finds a missed hazard.

holistic.reason: Union-co-designed, hazard-hold-safe, outage-tolerant counting rules and a baseline-verified pilot with a comparison group and friction removal make it approvable, but a team meal is a modest reward and the 'noticed' and 'lasting' effects depend on the default-screen redesign and technician buy-in.

claude.worst_flaw: The evaluation is a four-week before/after comparison that launches the workflow fixes and the team reward together, so it cannot show whether the reward added anything beyond plain queue support, and it sets no uncertainty or cost thresholds.

codex.worst_flaw: The pilot introduces the team reward alongside workflow changes without a reward-free comparison, so it cannot determine whether the reward improves review turnaround beyond what routing, protected time, and private feedback achieve.

holistic.reason: It fixes the queue and protects reviewer time before adding any reward, uses a team-level goal with no individual penalties and has a quality check, so sceptical engineers should accept it. codex.worst_flaw: The trial introduces the reward alongside better routing, protected review time, and private feedback, so it cannot tell whether the reward adds any value.

claude.worst_flaw: The trial changes the queue setup and adds the reward at the same time, then judges them only against a four-week before-and-after baseline, so it cannot tell whether the reward added anything beyond the routing fixes; it also has no appeal process or versioned record of the scoring rules.

holistic.reason: It fixes the actual queue bottlenecks first, uses a modest reward tied to a quality-audited metric, and plans a handoff to automatic routing, but the reward is low-salience and mostly private, and noticing depends on weekly channel posts and staying free of audit disputes.

claude.worst_flaw: The learning design is a four-week before/after comparison with no control or way to separate the gain from routing and protected review time from the gain from credits and reward, while managers can open individual cases and there is no morale check and no staffed appeal path, even though the engineers are already sceptical.

codex.worst_flaw: The pilot bundles workflow fixes, private feedback, and paid time off, so a higher on-time rate cannot show whether the reward adds value over the same workflow support and feedback alone.

holistic.reason: Fixes root-cause friction first, uses private feedback and a team-level reward with quality sampling, and plans to make routing defaults permanent, but the weekly sampling and manager visibility add overhead and some surveillance risk for sceptical engineers.

codex.worst_flaw: Without a concurrent ward using the same kiosk and feedback without the meal, the pilot cannot separate the reward’s effect from changes in staffing, workload, or familiarity with the kiosk.

claude.worst_flaw: The design judges success by comparing each ward with its own pre-reward month. holistic.reason: The design is thoughtful (workflow fixes, shared ward reward, audit reconciliation, pause rules), but it is complex to run, the reward depends on small audit samples, the privacy-sensitive code matching may erode trust, and the reward ends after only two cycles with no mechanism beyond the kiosk default to sustain logging.

codex.worst_flaw: The reward should wait until representative shadow scoring confirms that kiosk entries saved at a later break can be reliably matched to individual observed actions.

claude.worst_flaw: The design compares each ward only with its own before-and-after audits, with no comparison ward or plain-support arm and only a 30-action minimum, so it cannot separate the reward's effect from the workflow fixes, observer effects or secular trends.

holistic.reason: Unusually careful design that fixes workflow first, audits independently, separates recording from clinical compliance and has pause triggers, but the modest team-meal reward on a monthly audit cadence is low-salience, and lasting change depends on whether the kiosk becomes the default workflow rather than on the reward.

claude.worst_flaw: The pilot has no comparison condition, such as plain feedback versus the team meal or a non-pilot ward, so it cannot tell what the reward adds beyond the workflow fixes; it also has no staffed appeal process and no replayable record of events and policy versions.

codex.worst_flaw: A credible report that kiosk logging delayed patient care triggers a reward hold, with no rule requiring the ward to suspend logging while Infection Prevention investigates.

holistic.reason: The design is unusually rigorous on gaming risks, safety pauses, and separating kiosk logging from audited compliance, but sampling-based verification adds admin burden, the team-meal incentive is modest, and the eight-week plan hinges on the kiosk becoming the default workflow to sustain behavior after rewards end.

codex.worst_flaw: The before-and-after rollout bundles paid time with training, private feedback, and workflow changes, so it cannot establish whether the reward adds value.

claude.worst_flaw: There is no comparison group or incremental-value test. Success is judged by a before/after coverage rise against the baseline, so plain workflow fixes and the reward's own effect can't be separated, and no cost or harm decision thresholds are set ahead of time.

holistic.reason: Well-designed with fair per-agent targets, quality sampling, CSAT guardrails and a pre-launch pilot, but the 30-minute paid-time reward is modest against a 12% baseline, and the 50% target is a big jump that may rely on generic-link gaming and fade once rewards end.

codex.worst_flaw: The pilot lacks a feedback-only comparison, so any increase in coverage cannot establish whether the reward adds value beyond protected time, training, and workflow fixes.

claude.worst_flaw: The design has no comparison group or predefined decision criteria at a usable sample size, so a coverage rise from 12% can't be separated from the workflow fixes, the novelty effect or seasonal changes in ticket mix. holistic.reason: It fixes tool friction first, uses a clear per-ticket rule with audits and CSAT safeguards, and ends by making the workflow the default, but the reward is a small 45-minute paid block that agents may barely notice and goals may feel complex, so habit lasts only if the resolution-form defaults really cut the effort.

codex.worst_flaw: The pilot introduces the reward alongside workflow improvements and private feedback, so its before-and-after comparison cannot show whether the reward adds value.

claude.worst_flaw: There is no comparison group or predefined decision criteria with costs, so the design cannot separate the reward's added value from the workflow fix, and it relies on a before/after comparison against baseline.

holistic.reason: It fixes workflow friction first, rewards only real credit-worthy outcomes with a quality-sampling circuit breaker and a CSAT/reopen guard, but the one-hour time-off reward is modest, a 50% goal may feel distant from the 12% baseline, and lasting effect depends on the default-in-panel change surviving.
